title: Registered foreground focused cargo-test runs stay 'verification received, not settled' while cargo-check runs settle
outcome: A registered focused cargo-test launcher run that passes eligibly on the named root settles its verification onto the launch row the same way a cargo-check run does, or the host says why it stays received and what settles it.
acceptance: When Claude's Bash tool returns the output of a registered test-launcher run cut short (Claude Code persisted the full output), the host reads only the launcher's own locator lines (RUN, STARTED and results:) from the visible part of that output, validates each against the run directory on disk exactly as it does for uncut output, and attaches the run's artifact to the command's launch row; nothing else from cut output counts as evidence, and persisted output paths are never opened. A registered focused cargo-test run launched in the foreground whose output was cut, and which passed eligibly, then has its verification record settled rather than left received. Shown by a behaviour test with a cut foreground result.

When a registered test-launcher run started through Claude's Bash tool runs in the background, whether launched with run_in_background or moved there by the tool's time limit, the host attaches the run's artifact to the command's launch row when Claude reports that background task's end, taking the run directory and request identity from the run's host-owned registration. It attaches it only when exactly one registration of the row's session and worktree, with the row's launcher mode, started within the row's launch window and is carried by no other launch row, and it validates that registration's run directory on disk as for a console locator; otherwise it attaches nothing and records why. Persisted output paths are never opened. Such a run that passed eligibly then has its verification record settled rather than left received. Shown by behaviour tests for a run launched with run_in_background and for a run moved to the background by the time limit. C2 attaches only a terminal, uniquely matched registration read through the guarded run-directory reader; any other interleaving attaches nothing and records why. Interleavings in which the run directory's results change between the candidate read and the attachment, or in which a new competing registration or launch row appears during those reads, are outside this criterion and tracked separately. At a background task's end, a focused launch run through a shell wrapper (bash, sh or zsh -c, pwsh or powershell -Command, cmd /c) inside a Claude Bash line is not matched to a registration: it attaches nothing that way and records why; only a direct, unwrapped launcher command line is matched. A locator the launcher printed in that call's own output is associated as for any launcher. Registration matching compares the run's recorded focused command with the line's words as decoded by single quotes, double quotes, backslash escapes and backslash-newline continuation only, with no other shell quoting or expansion applied: when they are equal the registration is matched; when they differ it attaches nothing that way and records why. The line's own printed locator is associated as for any launcher.
